title: Assembly shift revision briefing
script: Revision C changes the connector step. To assemble, attend the morning briefing and sign the record. If you miss the briefing, label sealed boxes until the next session. Keep a clear paper trail. On the training sheet, cross out any mistake with one line and initial the correction. The line leader files that same sheet. Don’t copy signatures to a new page. Yesterday’s shortage is over. Fresh stock is cleared for assembly. Yesterday’s opened trays stay on the hold rack until Quality signs their tags. Keep the line working, but use cleared stock only.

questions.prompt: One worker attended but hasn’t signed. The other missed the briefing. How can both contribute now?

options.text: Have both workers assemble if they sign the record now.
Let the worker who attended start assembly now and send the other to label boxes.
Have the worker who attended sign, then assemble; send the other to label boxes.
Have both workers wait until the next briefing before doing any work.

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say, “Keep a clear paper trail”?

options.text: To make sure the latest sheet replaces all original records.
To let a later reviewer see the original entry and who corrected it.
To allow absent workers to reuse signatures that are already on file.
To prevent anyone from changing a training record after making a mistake.

questions.prompt: A model has only yesterday’s opened trays left. Another model has fresh stock. The tray tags are unsigned. What should the crew produce now?

options.text: Continue the first model because the shortage has been resolved.
Continue the first model after a line leader initials the tray tags.
Stop producing both models until the opened trays are cleared.
Build the other model with fresh stock and keep the opened trays on hold.
